headline_marked: [[Mob violence erupts in Noakhali]] over drug allegations, one killed in Sonaimuri
headline: Mob violence erupts in Noakhali over drug allegations, one killed in Sonaimuri
summary: Public outrage over drug-related incidents has led to a surge in vigilante attacks across Noakhali, with residents assaulting alleged drug dealers and vandalizing homes, resulting in one death.
details: In Noakhali's Sonaimuri upazila, Md. Foyez (37) was abducted from his home, beaten, and left critically injured by a group of locals on Thursday night. He was declared dead upon arrival at the Upazila Health Complex.
Foyez's father alleges his son was deliberately killed after being falsely accused of drug dealing. A murder case has been filed against 11 named individuals, and police have arrested two suspects.

This incident is part of a growing trend in Noakhali, where multiple individuals have been beaten and homes attacked over accusations of drug involvement. On Friday, a mob attacked the home of Md. Bodi in Begumganj, also accused of drug dealing, vandalizing his tin fence and boundary wall.

The same night, three individuals—Delwar Hossain, Md. Karim, and Alauddin—were detained and beaten by locals in Kabirhat upazila over alleged drug sales. A video circulating on Facebook shows an elderly man being beaten while pressed against an electric pole.

These attacks are reportedly linked to the killing of Arafat Hossain (15), a tenth-grade student, in Senbagh upazila on Wednesday night. Arafat was allegedly attacked and hacked by identified drug dealers after he and his relatives protested their use of his maternal grandparents' yard for drug activities.

Arafat succumbed to his injuries at Noakhali General Hospital. Police arrested the main suspect, Md. Harun, the same night, and a murder case was filed against seven individuals. The remaining suspects are yet to be apprehended.

The death of schoolboy Arafat sparked widespread anger on Facebook and among the general public in the district, leading to the subsequent vigilante actions against alleged drug dealers. Concerns are rising about the lack of effective police action contributing to a trend of "mobs" taking the law into their own hands.

Abu Naser Manju, General Secretary of Sujon's district committee, expressed concern, stating that while drug dealers are criminals, taking the law into one's own hands through assault, home attacks, or murder is unacceptable and shows disregard for the law. He urged conscious citizens to assist the police rather than resort to vigilantism.

Additional Superintendent of Police (Administration) Abu Tayeb Md. Arif Hossain acknowledged public anger against drug dealers and confirmed that instructions have been given to all police stations. He stated that police are vigilant to prevent anyone from creating an unstable environment by taking the law into their own hands, and investigations into the deaths in Senbagh and Sonaimuri are ongoing.

headline_marked: Prime Minister [[returns to Dhaka]] after day-long visit to Cox's Bazar
headline: Prime Minister returns to Dhaka after day-long visit to Cox's Bazar
summary: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina concluded her busy day in Cox's Bazar, participating in various development activities and public engagements before flying back to the capital.
details: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has returned to Dhaka following a comprehensive day-long visit to Cox's Bazar. Her visit focused on reviewing ongoing development projects and engaging with local communities.

During her time in Cox's Bazar, the Prime Minister participated in several key events. These included addressing a public rally, planting trees as part of an environmental initiative, and offering prayers.

The visit underscored the government's commitment to the development of the Cox's Bazar region, a vital area for tourism and economic growth. Such engagements allow direct interaction with citizens and assessment of ground-level progress.
